text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday: NEUE ZUERCHER ZEITUNG - Largest Swiss internet service provider Swiss Online announced plans to switch its services from state agency PTT Telecom to new private rival Newtelco's high speed network. Newtelco is the first privatly owned telecommunication network provider in Switzerland and is a joint venture of the Federal Railways, Union Bank of Switzerland and retailer Migros. - The percentage of foreigners living in Switzerland rose by 0.2 percentage points to 19 percent compared to the previous year. - Swiss Defence Minister Adolf Ogi will meet his American counterpart William Perry in Washington on Saturday. TAGES ANZEIGER - Swiss textile machine manufacturer Sulzer Rueti said it will axe 950 jobs in its plants in Rueti, Zuchwil and abroad. - Swiss Transport Minister Moritz Leuenberger opened a 19 kilometer motorway section creating the first direct motorway link between Zurich and Basle. After 30 years of planning and building, the section cost 1.12 billion Swiss francs. JOURNAL DE GENEVE - U.S. Senator Alfonso D'Amato said in an interview that he was determined to put further pressure for action on three separate bodies created within the past year in Switzerland to investigate the fate of Jewish funds that may have been left in Swiss banks by Holocaust victims. He also said he wanted to set up a new independent commission to keep tabns on the others. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
